wv_l_dr_ruth_s_big_buttress.blurb: A buttress along Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, mostly a trad venue with two bolted lines among its twelve routes. Grades run from 5.8 up to 5.13, but the bulk sit in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on sandstone gear routes who want a few harder tests nearby. The cracks and arete lines in the 5.9 and 5.10 range are the draw here and rank among the more sought-after lines on the wall. Reaching it means a short walk along the base from the neighbouring Snake Buttress, heading upstream, or dropping in from the rim and walking a little way down the cliff line.

wv_n_the_undeserved_area.blurb: A zone of Endless Wall in the New River Gorge that favours climbers carrying a trad rack: nine of its twelve routes are gear-protected and three are bolted. The sandstone is fine-grained and high quality, and the climbing is mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with one easy line near 5.6 and a single 5.9. Expect bold, classic lines rather than a beginner's cragging spot. Shade arrives on the cliff around midday or early afternoon. Getting in involves one of the ladder or cirque descents along the rim trail, or a rappel from the top that includes some exposed downclimbing, so check the base is clear before heading down.

wv_motorcycle_rocks.blurb: A small bouldering spot at Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia, built around two big boulders that the trail threads between, just beyond the no-climbing zone around the main overlook. Twelve sandstone problems cover a wide range: plenty of easy V0 to V4 lines, plus a handful of much harder ones reaching into the V7 to V9 range, a few of them standouts. It makes a quick add-on to a visit to the overlook area rather than a full-day destination. Keep off wet rock, and tidy up chalk and tick marks after your session.

wv_corrosion_block.blurb: A single big block in the Upper Rock City section of Coopers Rock State Forest, easy to spot by its tall roof split by a crack. Of its twelve lines, most are sandstone boulder problems from V0 to the V7 range, with several in the easy-to-moderate middle; two short top-rope routes and one 5.11 trad line add rope options. Low problems and easier taller routes make it friendly for mixed groups, though a few harder problems give stronger boulderers something to try. It sits close to the Tomb Raider slab and is reached from the main parking area on the Rattlesnake Trail.

wv_6_cambodia.blurb: A remote cliff in the Meadow River Gorge, part of the Upper Meadow zone of the New River Gorge region. It holds a dozen sandstone routes, eleven of them bolted and one trad, with grades from 5.8 up to 5.12. The majority fall between 5.11 and 5.12, so this is a spot for experienced sport climbers rather than beginners. The routes are vertical to just short of vertical. It involves a long, bushy walk-in along an old railroad grade, which keeps crowds away and rewards those who like solitude. It is best avoided in wet weather.
